messages:
maria: FYI CI eval-runner uploads started failing last night with 413s when traces > 10MB. Seen on a few model bring-ups and quantization runs.

upload-bot: [upload] failed for run 2026-03-19T23:40Z -> 413 Request Entity Too Large

jon: I pulled one of the failing payloads. Runner is sending a single gzipped file per-run. Some traces balloon to 40-60MB because we store full per-sample logits + token-level outputs inline. 413 from our CDN gateway (nginx) before it hits S3.

maria: example error from CI log: 
```
PUT https://uploads.redwood-inference.internal/eval-traces/2026-03-19/run-441
HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large
{"error":"EntityTooLarge"}
```

sasha: we should switch to either multipart uploads or upload per-sample objects + an index file. Proposal: schema v2 = index.json with minimal per-sample metadata + artifact_url for gzipped per-sample JSONL. That keeps run-level index small and lets us stream/download samples lazily. :+1:

sasha: example index entry (conceptual):
```
{
  "schema_version": "eval-trace-v2",
  "run_id": "run-441",
  "model": "redwood/ggml-13b-q4",
  "samples": [
    { "sample_id": "s-0001", "prompt_hash": "abc123", "token_count": 147, "latency_ms": 120, "artifact_url": "s3://.../run-441/s-0001.jsonl.gz", "artifact_size": 23456, "sha256": "..." }
  ]
}
```

kevin: uploading per-sample objects will raise PUT count and small-object costs. Tradeoff: cheaper egress/storage overall vs higher request pricing. We can mitigate with lifecycle rules and multipart upload where appropriate. Propose lifecycle: default 90d -> Glacier after 30d for non-flagged runs; allow tag `regression:keep` to extend to 180d.

tara: dashboard implications: we must avoid loading full trace into browser. Dashboard should fetch index.json and show per-sample metadata, with a link to download artifact (streamed). Also add a preview endpoint that returns sanitized sample for quick diffs.

maria: immediate runner changes I want: 1) gzip payloads (already done sometimes), 2) if gzip size > 5MB split into chunks, 3) support multipart S3 uploads with resume and exponential backoff, 4) fail CI fast if any single sample gz > 5MB and warn (we should avoid 1 huge sample). Also emit metrics: eval.upload_bytes, eval.upload_chunks, eval.upload_failures.

jon: will implement multipart + chunking. Also will add validation step before upload that computes per-sample gzipped size estimate and optionally writes samples as separate objects if they exceed threshold. I can add a feature flag `eval_runner/trace_chunking=true` for gradual rollouts.

sasha: I'll open a spec PR for eval-trace-schema v2 with the fields we discussed: run_id, schema_version, model, model_hash, dataset, commit_sha, started_at, completed_at, samples[]. Each sample entry: sample_id, prompt_hash, token_count, latency_ms, artifact_url, artifact_format(gzip/jsonl), artifact_size_bytes, sha256, labels(optional). Include top-level compression flag and a checksum for index.json. Backwards compatibility: old runners continue to upload v1; ingestion service should accept v1 and v2; v1 will be automatically converted to v2 on ingest if possible.

kevin: operational tasks I’ll take: update S3 lifecycle rules, add tagging for regression retention, and estimate cost delta for increased PUTs. Also add a CloudFront config tweak to allow larger uploads to S3 (configure nginx client_max_body_size + multipart proxying).

maria: alerting: add an SLO for upload success rate >= 99% over 1h for eval-runner; page if >5% failures for 5m. Also add Sentry error grouping for upload stack traces.

jon: noted on alerts. I'll add retries with jitter and exponential backoff and surface human-friendly error reasons in CI logs.

maria: owners and timelines: @sasha schema PR by EOD Wed, @jon runner multipart + chunking PR by Thu, @kevin infra lifecycle + CDN tweak by Fri, @tara dashboard changes queued for next sprint but add index previews this week. We'll aim to enable chunking behind feature flag next Tue and flip on by Fri if no regressions. :calendar:

tara: I'll add UI placeholders and a server-side preview endpoint that returns the first non-sensitive fields only.

kevin: also recommendation: tag traces with `sensitivity=low|medium|high` so retention and preview redact accordingly.

maria: perfect. I'll write a short postmortem-style note in #postmortems after we ship changes. Thanks all. :pray:
